summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and recent history of an infected AV graft presented with lethargy and a 4-point drop in hematocrit. He was transfused one unit of packed red blood cells, which improved his hematocrit to 31.8. Evaluation did not reveal active gastrointestinal bleeding, hemolysis, or acute cardiac injury, though new T-wave inversions were noted on EKG. He received three hours of hemodialysis during admission. His wife raised concerns about worsening depression, including poor sleep, low energy, and decreased appetite, and he was advised to discuss switching from sedating mirtazapine to a non-sedating antidepressant with his primary care provider. He was discharged home on unchanged medications, including ongoing cefazolin for recent graft infection, with recommendations to follow up on colonoscopy and monitor daily weight for fluid changes.
